Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i think we're all set. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Ethan, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Laura Kim: Good morning, hey thanks for setting this up. We just wanted a short discovery to understand the quickstart/workflow—particularly free credits and how fast we can get to first token.
[00:15] Ethan Ross: Awesome, that's a great place to start. We'll run through the PLG quickstart, what the hosted API experience looks like, and then chat about dedicated/private if you have enterprise constraints.
[00:28] Daniel Ortiz: Quick note — we care about latency tail and cost per token. We'll probably start with some frontend assistant use cases then scale to embedding/semantic search.
[00:36] Priya Shah: And security is a blocker for us—SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs. If Redwood has a private option we'd like to understand the tradeoffs.
[00:44] Maya Patel: Totally. Quick agenda: 1) quickstart flow and free credits, 2) hosted API capabilities and SLAs, 3) dedicated & private overview, 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:50] Laura Kim: Yep.
[00:52] Ethan Ross: Kicking off the quickstart — from signup to first token we typically see teams at ~15-60 minutes if they follow the quickstart. Quickstart gives free credits, a sample curl and SDK snippets. The hosted API supports text generation, chat, embeddings.
[01:10] Maya Patel: We include starter templates and a free trial credit — that credit can be used on hosted inference. No credit card on file is required for the quickstart in most regions.
[01:19] Daniel Ortiz: Can you send the exact docs? Also curious if we can spin up a dedicated pool quickly for predictable throughput.
[01:26] Ethan Ross: I'll share the quickstart doc and our benchmark spreadsheet — that shows latency numbers across models. Dedicated is a reserved capacity product; provisioning depends on region and commit but we can spin a test pool for POC with short-term reserved infra; typically a few days to setup for Dedicated POC.
[01:45] Priya Shah: For private/on-prem, what are the constraints? We have some regulated data so may need VPC or on-prem later.
[01:50] Ethan Ross: Private offers a customer-managed control plane and on-prem packaging. It includes KMS integrations and audit logs. There's an enterprise sales cycle—approx timelines vary; for pilot you can start hosted and then migrate to private/dedicated.
[02:05] Laura Kim: Great. What's the difference in latency/cost between hosted and dedicated?
[02:10] Ethan Ross: Hosted is very convenient and often cheaper at low volume due to pooled utilization. Dedicated gives lower tail latency predictability and better isolation for consistent high throughput — cost model shifts to reserved capacity. Also dedicated lets you pin quantization profiles and kernel choices to squeeze cost.
[02:30] Daniel Ortiz: We run at ~100 QPS peak for chat use—do you have guidance on batching vs latency tradeoffs?
[02:36] Ethan Ross: Yes — we can tune batching, KV-prefix caching, and micro-batching. For real-time chat, we bias toward smaller batch windows to preserve latency. For async bulk embeddings, you batch large. We'll include recommended configs based on your expected sequence length.
[02:56] Maya Patel: Quick FYI — we have a model catalog with verified perf profiles; we'll point you to models that match low-latency vs high-quality tradeoffs.
[03:05] Laura Kim: On security: do you have SOC2, ISO docs? Does Redwood support SSO/SAML?
[03:10] Maya Patel: Yes, SOC2 compliant, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS integrations. We'll share our security pack (redwood_security_packet.pdf) and you can loop in your InfoSec.
[03:20] Priya Shah: Does the hosted API see our data? What's retention?
[03:24] Ethan Ross: By default hosted inference processes requests without persistent training; logs/audit retention can be configured. For regulated data we recommend Private deployment or strict contract terms. We'll include our data retention docs in the security pack.
[03:39] Daniel Ortiz: About time-to-first-token — can you walk through a sample curl? We want to measure from signup to a 1-token response.
[03:45] Ethan Ross: Sure — sample flow: signup, get API key, run sample curl with model=redwood-1-small (or an open model), you should get a token stream within <200ms server-side on average for small models in hosted env. We'll share the exact curl and a script to measure TTF.
[04:05] Laura Kim: That would help. Also curious if we can get a short free pilot for our team to run our prompt set.
[04:11] Maya Patel: We usually offer trial credits that you can apply to a pilot. For more targeted pilots we can do a short POC with dedicated test pool and benchmark support — that's typically sales-assisted and requires a quick scoping call.
[04:27] Daniel Ortiz: What about rate limits? We might have bursty traffic.
[04:30] Ethan Ross: Hosted has per-account rate limits and adjustable quotas; for bursty but low sustained traffic it works well. For high sustained throughput you want Dedicated where you define capacity and autoscaling policies, plus burst buffers.
[04:45] Priya Shah: Any compliance for EU data residency? We operate in NA/EU — need to ensure data doesn't leave region.
[04:52] Maya Patel: We have region-aware routing and can deploy private/dedicated in EU regions. For strict residency, Private with customer-managed VPC is recommended. We'll include region routing details.
[05:05] Laura Kim: What's the onboarding process — do you have a quickstart checklist?
[05:09] Maya Patel: Yes — signup, allocate trial credits, run quickstart curl, choose model, run sample prompt set, measure latency/cost. I'll send the checklist and a starter repo.
[05:20] [crosstalk] Daniel Ortiz: (mumble) okay good —
[05:25] Ethan Ross: I'll also attach benchmark CSV with numbers across redwood-1-small/medium and quantized variants so you can estimate cost per 1k tokens.
[05:36] Priya Shah: For the SI/infra team, we may want a technical deep dive on quantization and kernel selection — can your SE cover that?
[05:42] Ethan Ross: Absolutely — SE deep dive covers runtime, KV cache, compilation behavior, and quantization guidance. We'll plan that as a follow-up if you confirm the pilot.
[05:55] Laura Kim: Any typical blockers you see for teams starting self-serve?
[05:58] Maya Patel: Mostly team access and security approvals. Time-to-first-token is often fast; the blocker is InfoSec approval for hosted. For that we hand over the security packet and offer private POC if needed.
[06:12] Daniel Ortiz: Ok makes sense. If we start with hosted quickstart, do we have an SLA?
[06:16] Maya Patel: Hosted is best-effort for free-tier; paid hosted customers get defined SLAs. Dedicated/Private are where we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets.
[06:27] Priya Shah: Pricing ask — send us a ballpark for hosted usage and a dedicated starter config.
[06:31] Maya Patel: We'll send ballpark numbers and examples (cost per 1M tokens, dedicated monthly reserve for X GPUs).
[06:40] Ethan Ross: One more technical note: if you want to minimize latency we recommend pinning model variants, enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts, and using our streaming API. We'll include config snippets.
[06:54] Laura Kim: Sounds good. Timeline-wise we want to have a pilot decision by next Thursday 3/11.
[06:59] Maya Patel: Great — we'll aim to get the materials over by Friday 3/6 and schedule an SE deep dive week of 3/9.
[07:08] Daniel Ortiz: Perfect. Any docs/links you want us to look at before the deep dive?
[07:11] Maya Patel: Quickstart guide link (will send), security packet (will send), benchmark spreadsheet (will send). Also a short sample app repo.
[07:19] Priya Shah: Ok thanks — that should help our InfoSec as well.
[07:22] [brief pause]
[07:28] Maya Patel: Recap: we'll send quickstart + trial credit setup, sample curl & benchmark CSV, pricing ballparks, and security packet. Action items noted. Plan SE deep dive the week of 3/9 pending pilot sign-off.
[07:44] Laura Kim: Thanks everyone, appreciate it. We'll follow up internally and share our prompt set.
[07:49] Maya Patel: Thanks all, talk soon.
